s1.syndrome_frame: Persistent painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition on the hand following a twisting injury
salient_findings: Painful bruise on the hand that persisted despite icing and resting
Ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque on the dorsum of the left hand
Heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion on MRI
key_facts: The patient is a woman in her 30s
The bruise appeared a few days after a twisting injury to the hand
The bruise and pain have persisted for 2 years
The patient denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
Radiography showed soft tissue swelling but was otherwise unremarkable
MRI showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense lesion
Pathology showed mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli
Immunohistochemistry was strongly positive for CD34 and negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A

shortlist.label: Hemosiderotic fibrohistiocytic lipomatous lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling and pigment deposition

shortlist.label: Nora lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical and histological features align with the case, including the presence of a painful bruise and mixed fibrous and adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Post-traumatic fat necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: History of twisting injury and persistence of bruise and pain for 2 years support this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Morel-Lavallee lesion
shortlist.why_kept: Closed degloving injury with a history of trauma and presence of a painful bruise with soft tissue swelling

shortlist.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, the presence of pigment deposition and a history of trauma make this a plausible, albeit rare, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The lesion's mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition, along with the presence of spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid cells and strong positivity for CD34, are characteristic of a hemosiderotic fibrohistiocytic lipomatous lesion.

rejected.label: Nora lesion
rejected.why: Nora lesion typically presents as a painless, slow-growing mass, which does not match the patient's painful bruise and persistent pain.

rejected.label: Post-traumatic fat necrosis
rejected.why: Post-traumatic fat necrosis usually occurs in areas with abundant subcutaneous fat and does not typically show the same level of fibrohistiocytic proliferation and hemosiderin deposition as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Morel-Lavallee lesion
rejected.why: Morel-Lavallee lesion is a closed degloving injury that typically occurs in the context of severe trauma, which is not consistent with the patient's twisting injury during acroyoga.

rejected.label: Pigmented villonodular synovitis
rejected.why: Pigmented villonodular synovitis is a synovial-based lesion that typically affects the joints, which does not match the subcutaneous location of the lesion in this case.
